title: Growth GARP research: top 5 Nordic and top 10 global

files.name: Amazon.com Inc
files.businessSummary: E-commerce and third-party marketplace retailer; AWS cloud computing; advertising; devices and subscriptions (Prime).

netDebt.note: Total debt $304,841M less cash & investments $114,226M; fulfillment-center lease treatment unconfirmed.

enterpriseValue.note: Mixes Nov price with Sep balance sheet.

fcfTTM.note: Operating CF $168,300M minus capex $215,192M; capex has roughly doubled YoY on AI/data-center buildout.

fcfYield.note: Negative FCF yield -- flag for a GARP screen.

recentEvents: Q3 2025 results: AWS growth reaccelerated; retail and advertising also grew; EPS beat and AWS reacceleration cited as catalysts for a sharp stock rise.
valueTrapFlags: TTM FCF sharply negative (-$46.9B) vs +$7.7B FY2025 and +$32.9B FY2024 -- capex more than doubled for AI/data-center buildout.
Operating cash flow growing (+21% FY2025 to TTM) but entirely outrun by capex -- FCF conversion has collapsed.
No dividend, so payout-based leverage checks n/a.
growthQualityNotes: Revenue growth real, steady, recent: $469.8B (FY2021) to $716.9B (FY2025), ~11%/yr.
Operating margin genuinely expanding: trough 2.6% (FY2022) to 11.15% (FY2025).
Path to sustained positive FCF has REVERSED in the most recent TTM due to the AI capex supercycle -- key watch item.
AMZN absent from the stock-agent feed -- no secondary cross-check available.
dataGaps: Forward P/E, EV/EBIT forward, ND/EBITDA, interest coverage, historical multiple range, itemized forward estimates, stock-agent cross-check unavailable.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS; the sharply negative TTM FCF (AI capex supercycle) is treated as a risk/quality flag rather than built into the basis value

bear.note: AI capex keeps outrunning operating cash flow for longer than expected, margin story stalls.

base.note: AWS reaccelerates as AI capex starts converting to revenue, retail/advertising margins keep expanding.

bull.note: AWS AI infrastructure monetizes faster than expected, FCF reinflects as capex growth moderates.

valuation.whyItFits: Genuine, steady multi-year revenue growth and real operating-margin expansion (2.6% to 11.15%) across retail, advertising and AWS, but the current AI capex supercycle has temporarily reversed free cash flow -- the central open question for this GARP case.
valuation.growthDrivers: AWS AI infrastructure/compute demand, retail logistics efficiency, advertising growth.
valuation.saturation: No saturation in revenue growth; the constraint right now is capital intensity (capex), not demand.
valuation.principalRisk: If AI infrastructure capex does not convert to AWS revenue growth as expected, the current negative free cash flow becomes a structural rather than cyclical problem.

files.name: ASML Holding N.V.
files.businessSummary: Sole supplier of EUV lithography systems and a leading supplier of DUV systems to leading-edge semiconductor manufacturers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, etc.).

price.note: EUR, Amsterdam listing. stock-agent showed 1,406.79 for ticker 'ASML' (presumably the Nasdaq USD ADR) -- not reconciled.

sharesOutstanding.note: ~382M implied by market cap/price, not independently confirmed.

netDebt.note: stock-agent ND/EBITDA of -0.67 implies net cash; underlying EUR figure not independently fetched.

enterpriseValue.note: unavailable without a verified net cash figure.

dividendPerShare.note: Q3 2025 interim EUR1.60 confirmed via asml.com press release.

forwardEstimates.source: company guidance: ~15% FY2025 sales growth vs 2024; does not expect 2026 below 2025

recentEvents: Q3 2025: net sales EUR7,516M, net income EUR2,125M, gross margin 51.6%.
Q3 2025 net bookings EUR5,399M, of which EUR3.6B EUV.
Q4 2025 guidance: net sales EUR9,200-9,800M, gross margin 51-53%.
EUR12B 2022-2025 buyback program under-run (only EUR5.9B executed as of Sep 2025); new program to be announced Jan 2026.
valueTrapFlags: Buyback materially behind its own pace/size -- capital-allocation signal to watch.
FY2023 FCF dipped sharply despite revenue growth that year -- working-capital timing issue.
Heavy dependence on a small number of leading-edge customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel).
growthQualityNotes: Revenue growth real: EUR18.6B (FY2021) to EUR32.7B (FY2025), including a near-flat FY2023-24 downcycle then FY2025 reacceleration.
Operating margin range-bound (31-35%) rather than steadily expanding -- a stable-margin, not margin-expansion, story.
FCF volatile due to lumpy working capital tied to large system shipments, but TTM/FY2025 level (~EUR10-11B) suggests durable positive FCF.
dataGaps: Shares outstanding, net debt in EUR, EV, EV/EBIT, EV/EBITDA (stock-agent figure discarded), ROIC, ROE, interest coverage, historical multiple range unavailable.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS (EUR), reflecting ASML's range-bound (not expanding) margin profile and lumpy FCF

bear.note: Semiconductor-equipment downcycle repeats (as in FY2023-24), EUV capex delayed by customers.

base.note: AI-driven leading-edge capex continues at a steady pace, similar to the FY2025 reacceleration.

bull.note: AI chip demand drives an extended leading-edge capex upcycle, High-NA EUV adoption accelerates.

valuation.whyItFits: Sole supplier of EUV lithography with effectively no credible competitor, real recent revenue reacceleration (FY2025 +15.6%) after the FY2023-24 downcycle, strong net-cash balance sheet -- the cleanest 'structural moat' growth case on the shortlist, even though margins aren't expanding, just stable.
valuation.growthDrivers: AI/leading-edge semiconductor capex, High-NA EUV system adoption, structural industry reliance on ASML's monopoly position.
valuation.saturation: The FY2023-24 near-flat period shows this is a cyclical-within-structural-growth business -- capex cycles will keep causing lumpiness.
valuation.principalRisk: Heavy dependence on a small number of leading-edge customers (TSMC, Samsung, Intel); a slowdown in their capex plans would hit ASML directly, and geopolitical export restrictions remain a standing risk.

files.name: Broadcom Inc
files.businessSummary: Designer of semiconductors (networking, custom AI ASICs, broadband) and, since the 2023 VMware acquisition, a large enterprise infrastructure software business.

price.note: CONFLICT: stock-agent showed $333.40 for a nearby date, unreconciled.

netDebt.note: Total debt $59,419M less cash & investments $23,975M; lease treatment unconfirmed.

enterpriseValue.note: Mixes Nov price with Aug balance sheet.

recentEvents: Q4/FY2025 results (~Dec 2025): revenue $18,015M Q4, +28% YoY; AI/custom-silicon and VMware software cited as growth drivers; shares reportedly fell post-earnings despite the beat.
valueTrapFlags: FY2024 operating margin dipped sharply and net income collapsed -- VMware acquisition costs/amortization, not organic deterioration.
Reported negative share-price reaction to the latest beat suggests the market may price flawless execution.
Trailing P/E (~44x) and EV/EBITDA (~32x) both rich and conflicting slightly between sources.
growthQualityNotes: Revenue growth real: $27.5B (FY2021) to $63.9B (FY2025), mixed organic/inorganic (VMware).
Margin trend distorted by the VMware deal; FY2025 recovery is partial normalization plus AI mix benefit.
Already solidly FCF positive and growing, with high ROIC (~31%) and ROE (~44%).
dataGaps: Forward P/E, EV/EBIT forward, interest coverage, historical multiple range, itemized forward estimates not found.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS, with the VMware-related FY2024 margin distortion explicitly normalized out of the growth assumption

bear.note: Custom AI ASIC demand slows, VMware integration synergies underwhelm, multiple compresses from today's ~44x.

base.note: AI networking/custom-silicon and VMware software both grow steadily, similar to today's multiple.

bull.note: Custom AI silicon wins accelerate (additional hyperscaler customers), VMware software margins keep expanding.

valuation.whyItFits: Real growth (networking/custom AI ASICs plus VMware software) with high ROIC (~31%) and ROE (~44%), though the growth is a mix of organic AI demand and the VMware acquisition rather than a single clean growth driver.
valuation.growthDrivers: Custom AI accelerator (ASIC) design wins with hyperscalers, VMware enterprise software cross-sell, networking silicon demand.
valuation.saturation: No clear saturation yet, but the market's negative reaction to a recent earnings beat suggests high expectations are already embedded.
valuation.principalRisk: FY2024's sharp margin/earnings dip (VMware acquisition costs) shows integration risk is real; a similar disruption from a future large acquisition, or AI-ASIC demand normalizing, would hit the growth case.

Redeye (via Borsvarlden): expects EBIT margin to keep expanding; US launch of CERAMENT G 'so-far highly successful.'
Stock fell ~6.1% despite strong Q3 print per simplywall.st -- worth noting.

bear.note: US CERAMENT G rollout slows, valuation multiple fully normalizes toward peer medtech levels.

bull.note: CERAMENT G US adoption accelerates sharply, international expansion adds further upside.

valuation.whyItFits: Genuine, high-margin (92% gross margin) revenue growth with a real recent profitability inflection and a currently 'highly successful' US launch per independent analyst commentary -- strongest pure growth quality of the Nordic names, but also the richest multiple and least data-verified price.
valuation.growthDrivers: US launch of CERAMENT G, international orthobiologics adoption, high (92%) gross margins giving strong operating leverage.
valuation.saturation: None evident -- still early in the US commercial ramp.
valuation.principalRisk: A negative share-price reaction to an apparently strong Q3 print, plus an unresolved FY2023 EPS anomaly, suggest the market (or the data) may be seeing something not fully captured here; valuation leaves little room for a stumble.

files.name: Globus Medical, Inc.
files.businessSummary: Musculoskeletal healthcare products: spine fusion implants, motion preservation, interventional treatments, enabling technologies (robotics/navigation), and (via Nevro) neuromodulation.

price.note: Predates the Nov 7, 2026 Q3 earnings print and guidance cut.

recentEvents: Q3 2026 (reported ~Nov 7, 2026): FY2026 revenue guidance cut to $3.09bn from prior $3.18-3.22bn.
US Spine revenue grew only 2% in Q3 2026 vs a tough prior-year comp; international revenue fell 5.7%.
Despite the revenue cut, FY adjusted diluted EPS guidance held at $4.95-5.05 (implying 24.4-26.9% YoY growth).
Board increased share buyback authorization by $500 million concurrent with the guidance cut.
Enabling Technologies revenue +24% and robotic/navigation deployments +73% partially offset spine softness.
valueTrapFlags: Revenue guidance cut while EPS guidance held flat via margin discipline and a larger buyback -- EPS propped up, not organic growth.
Core US Spine growth decelerated sharply (2%) and international revenue declined (-5.7%).
Analyst consensus/targets predate the Nov 2026 guidance cut and are stale.
growthQualityNotes: Multi-year revenue growth real but uneven (7%, 53%, 61%, 17%, now decelerating further per the cut).
Gross margin drifted down from ~75% to ~68-69%; mild compression.
Operating margin recovered to a TTM high (23.2%) via cost discipline, not revenue leverage.
FCF yield modest (6.9%) and already positive.
dataGaps: Consensus pre-dates the Nov 7 guidance cut -- should be re-verified.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS, explicitly discounted for the Nov 2026 guidance cut and EPS-via-buyback dynamic

bear.note: US Spine and international declines persist; EPS support from buybacks runs out of room.

base.note: Spine stabilizes, Enabling Technologies (+24%) and robotics (+73%) keep offsetting the soft core.

bull.note: Robotics/navigation adoption accelerates meaningfully, reversing the Spine deceleration.

valuation.whyItFits: Robotics/navigation (Enabling Technologies) is a real, fast-growing (+24%, deployments +73%) structural growth driver inside an otherwise decelerating core Spine business -- included as a flagged, lower-conviction growth name given the Nov 7 guidance cut.
valuation.growthDrivers: Robotic/navigation surgical system adoption, Enabling Technologies segment growth, post-Nevro neuromodulation cross-sell.
valuation.saturation: Core US Spine growth has decelerated to 2% and international revenue is now declining -- the original growth engine is clearly maturing/competing harder.
valuation.principalRisk: EPS guidance is currently being held up by cost discipline and buybacks rather than organic growth; if that support is exhausted before Enabling Technologies scales enough, EPS could disappoint materially.

files.name: HEICO Corporation
files.businessSummary: Aerospace, defense and electronics products/services via Flight Support Group (jet engine/aircraft replacement parts, insulation, repair services) and Electronic Technologies Group.

valueTrapFlags: Extremely rich valuation: trailing P/E ~55x, forward ~48x, EV/EBIT ~35x, EV/EBITDA ~30x -- priced for flawless execution.
FCF yield low (2.5%) relative to the multiple.
Highest leverage of the names reviewed: ND/EBITDA 1.56x (actual debt).
~12% unreconciled price discrepancy between two data pulls -- ratios may understate current valuation.
growthQualityNotes: Strong, consistent multi-year revenue growth: $1.87bn (FY2021) to $5.18bn TTM.
Operating margin expanded steadily: 21.1% to 24.3% TTM.

Solidly FCF positive already; concern is valuation/leverage, not growth quality.
dataGaps: Payout ratio, interest coverage not confirmed.

valuation.method: EPS-based scenario fair value off TTM EPS, explicitly reflecting the already-rich valuation and thin FCF yield

bear.note: Aerospace aftermarket demand softens, high trailing multiple compresses toward a still-rich 30x.

valuation.growthDrivers: Aftermarket aerospace parts demand, continued bolt-on M&A, Electronic Technologies defense-electronics growth.
valuation.saturation: No clear saturation signal in the data, but the valuation already assumes the compounding continues without interruption.
valuation.principalRisk: At ~55x trailing earnings with a thin FCF yield (2.5%) and the highest leverage of the shortlist, any growth disappointment would trigger an outsized multiple de-rating.
